articles.title: ED Raids 13 Sites in Probe Into Fraudulent NRI Housing Loans
articles.excerpt: The Enforcement Directorate searched premises linked to Antriksh Promoters and Sunshine Infrawell across Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru and Chandigarh over housing loans allegedly obtained in NRIs' names with forged documents.
articles.nri_angle: The alleged fraud used NRIs' names and documents for India housing loans; NRIs borrowing or buying in India should verify loan accounts and authorisations directly with their lender.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Administration Narrows H-1B Hiring With Layoff Scrutiny and New Fees
articles.excerpt: A September 18 executive order makes an employer's layoffs in the past year a factor in H-1B reviews, alongside an extended $100,000 payment for hires from abroad and a proposal to end the 60-day job-loss grace period.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals hold a large share of H-1B visas in technology; layoff-linked scrutiny, the extended $100,000 payment and the proposed end of the 60-day grace period directly affect their employers' filings and their own job-loss timelines.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.card_title: Impact of Layoffs on H-1B Applications

articles.title: Social Security Faces 2032 Depletion as Congress Weighs Costly Fixes
articles.excerpt: The trustees project the retirement fund will pay only 78% of benefits after late 2032, while a budget rule could hide the cost of borrowing to pay benefits in full.
articles.nri_angle: Indian immigrant workers who have paid US payroll taxes for a decade or more face the same projected 22% retirement benefit cut in 2032 as other beneficiaries if Congress does not act.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian EB-2 Queue Stays Frozen in 2013 as Premium Processing Rule Reaches White House
articles.excerpt: The November 2026 Visa Bulletin held India's EB-2 final action date at November 1, 2013 for a second month, while a USCIS proposal to amend premium processing timeframes entered OIRA review on October 13 with its text still secret.
articles.nri_angle: Indian EB-2 applicants are the largest group in the US employment-based green card backlog; the frozen 2013 cutoff and any change to premium processing deadlines directly affect H-1B workers and their employers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indians Posted to UK Now Avoid Double Social Security for Five Years
articles.excerpt: The Double Contributions Convention, in force since July 15, extends the NIC exemption for detached workers from 52 weeks to 60 months — if they hold an EPFO Certificate of Coverage.
articles.image_caption: 10 Downing Street in London. Indians posted to the UK will now avoid double social security contributions for five years under the new agreement.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals posted to the UK by an India-based employer for up to 60 months now pay EPF at home instead of UK NICs, with no UK State Pension accrual during the posting.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Visa Fraud Crackdown Widens: Nine Universities Probed Over J-1, Outsourcers Suspended
articles.excerpt: Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito's campaign now spans an H-1B criminal probe, J-1 subpoenas to Harvard, MIT and seven other universities, PERM suspensions for Microsoft, Adobe and six IT outsourcers, and a new Visa Fraud Strike Team.
articles.nri_angle: Indians are 71% of H-1B beneficiaries and a large share of J-1 researchers and physicians; the crackdown changes the enforcement climate — frozen PERM pipelines at major employers, fraud-focused scrutiny — without changing any visa rule itself.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Diaspora Could Pay Price for West's Immigration Backlash, Sareen Warns
articles.excerpt: Speaking on Faultline, Sushant Sareen said communities with a long record of legal migration and integration could still be caught by visa tightening and scrutiny aimed at migration in general.
articles.image_caption: Faultline key art: Sushant Sareen (right), strategic affairs expert, in the Times Axis episode on the West's immigration backlash, with host Ananya Dasgupta (left).
articles.nri_angle: The warning is aimed directly at the diaspora: Sareen argues Indians who migrated legally could face tighter visas and greater scrutiny as Western politics turns against migration in general.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-American Immigration Debate Sharpens Over Assimilation, Scale and Culture in America
articles.excerpt: Christopher Rufo argues Indian Americans assimilate strongly but immigration should slow to match assimilation capacity. Critics quoted by CNN argue the “Indian question” framing otherizes the community and risks real-world harm.

sources.label: Christopher Rufo — The Indian-American Immigration Debate (City Journal essay)

articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans are the direct subject of this debate: Rufo argues the community assimilates strongly while urging slower immigration overall, and critics argue the framing itself exposes South Asian families, students and workers to increased hostility.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Minneapolis Café That Offered Free Meals Protesting ICE to Close Permanently
articles.excerpt: Modern Times Café, rebranded Post Modern Times, removed prices in January and barred ICE in protest at enforcement in Minnesota. Owner Dylan Alverson says he has exhausted every option and will close the 16-year-old business by the end of 2026.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian-American families and restaurant workers in Minneapolis, a café that made meal service a protest against ICE is closing on a business timeline, not a policy one — its 25-free-meals-a-day program ends with the business by the end of 2026, with no successor named.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Café reopened with prices and 25 free meals.

articles.title: Cloudera Pays $2 Million, Accepts Two-Year PERM Ban in US Worker Discrimination Settlement
articles.excerpt: The Justice and Labor departments say Cloudera directed PERM applicants to a non-functional email address, failed to consider qualified US workers for seven jobs, and must now fund $1.4 million in back pay, pay $600,000 in penalties and stay out of PERM for two years.

sources.label: US Department of Justice — Settlements and Lawsuits (IER)

articles.nri_angle: Cloudera's two-year PERM debarment freezes new green-card labor certifications at the company, directly affecting its Indian H-1B employees' permanent-residency timelines, and signals stricter PERM recruitment enforcement for all tech employers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two London Pharmacists Jailed Six Years Each Over £1.3 Million NHS Fraud
articles.excerpt: Jignesh Patel, 46, and Rahil Patel, 42, were sentenced at Southwark Crown Court on 16 October after 1,639 false prescriptions were used to obtain high-cost leukaemia drugs that were sold to wholesalers in Europe.
articles.nri_angle: Two British pharmacists of Indian origin were jailed in London for defrauding the NHS; UK diaspora readers can report suspected NHS fraud anonymously on the NHSCFA's 0800 028 4060 line.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.name: Payment from EU wholesaler for Noxafil

articles.title: Trump's Green Card Curbs Test Indian Tech Workers as PERM Freeze Hits Eight Firms
articles.excerpt: Nearly one million Indians are already waiting in the employment-based green card queue. A PERM suspension at Microsoft, Infosys, TCS and five other major employers now freezes the first step of the process for their staff.
articles.image_caption: US President Donald Trump. His administration's green card curbs are testing Indian tech workers as the PERM freeze hits eight firms.
articles.nri_angle: The PERM freeze directly affects Indian H-1B workers at eight major employers, most of whom are already in a green card queue where Indians hold 79% of pending cases.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.label: Indian nationals waiting for green cards
Projected wait times for highly skilled Indians

articles.title: Seven Countries Drive Most UK Study Visa Refusals as 5% Cap Reshapes Admissions
articles.excerpt: Home Office data to June 2026 show refusals concentrated in Pakistan, Nigeria and India, with universities withdrawing offers to protect their sponsor licences under the tightened compliance threshold.
articles.nri_angle: Indian applicants face a 4.4 per cent refusal rate just under the sponsor threshold, but withdrawals rose to 5.2 per cent and applications fell 31 per cent — check a university's BCA position before paying a deposit.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Justice Department Lets Stand Ruling That H-1B-Only Job Ads Are Not Illegal Alone
articles.excerpt: An administrative ruling dismissing a complaint over a Chicago H-1B jobs board survives after Attorney General Todd Blanche declined review, narrowing how targeted ads can be challenged.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals are over 70 per cent of H-1B holders; the ruling means a targeted ad alone is not actionable — a claimant must show harm in an actual hiring, recruitment or termination decision.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Federal Workers Face Capped Top Ratings as Tougher Reviews Roll Out
articles.excerpt: A new forced-distribution system limits ratings of 4 or 5 to 40% of staff, puts senior panels in charge of calibration, and leaves managers and employees warning of a hit to morale.
articles.nri_angle: Many Indian Americans and immigrants work in federal agencies; the capped ratings affect their bonuses, promotion prospects and retention standing in any future reduction in force.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: OPM directed agencies on rating limits

articles.title: DHS Final Rule Permanently Ends Automatic Work Permit Extensions For Renewals
articles.excerpt: The October 14, 2026 rule makes permanent the loss of the 540-day EAD bridge for renewals filed on or after October 30, 2025, hitting H-4 spouses and green card applicants who must now get approval before their card expires.
articles.image_caption: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security, which issued the final rule ending automatic work-permit extensions.
articles.nri_angle: Indian H-4 spouses and employment-based green card applicants spend years renewing EADs because of per-country backlogs, so losing the 540-day automatic bridge turns any USCIS delay into a direct risk of a forced break from work.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.label: Interim rule / cutoff for renewals losing auto-extension
Final rule published in Federal Register (91 Fed. Reg. 65306)

articles.title: Schweikert SMARTER Act Would Replace H-1B Lottery With Merit Points System
articles.excerpt: Arizona Republican's H.R. 10460 would scrap the lottery, set an initial 85,000 cap under a new board, and remove per-country green card caps — but it remains in committee, not law.
articles.image_caption: U.S. Representative David Schweikert, sponsor of the proposed SMARTER Act.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals receive the largest share of H-1B visas and face the longest green card backlogs, so replacing the lottery with points and removing per-country caps would directly reshape their path to work and residency in the U.S.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Labor Department Freezes PERM Green-Card Filings for Microsoft, Adobe, Six IT Firms
articles.excerpt: The October 8 suspension stops new and pending PERM labor certifications for eight employers under investigation. It does not cancel H-1B visas, and no fraud finding or written end date has been published.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals at the named IT firms and Microsoft, many on H-1B visas with PERM cases pending or planned, face a stalled green-card step while their current work status remains unchanged.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Proposed Immigration Court Contempt Rule Would Fine Lawyers Who Allege Bias
articles.excerpt: EOIR's proposed contempt penalties of up to $3,500 would cover private attorneys, respondents, and witnesses but exempt government attorneys. AILA urges withdrawal; supporters say judges have lacked an accountability tool since 1996.
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals and other diaspora families in removal or asylum proceedings depend on counsel being able to raise bias and due-process objections on the record; a penalty regime that exempts government lawyers affects how those cases are defended.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: AILA submitted comment opposing the rule

articles.title: US Proposes $70,000 OPT Fee That Could Hit Indian Students Hardest
articles.excerpt: A DHS proposal would charge universities $70,000 for a student's first OPT recommendation and $30,000 for any subsequent OPT, including STEM extensions. It is not in effect, and comments close November 9, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Indian students are the largest international student group in the US and the largest OPT cohort, so a $70,000 school-paid fee that may be passed on to students directly affects Indian families budgeting for US study.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.label: Total for Pre and Post Completion

articles.title: ICE Detains Bronx Food Pantry Founder After Court Hearing, and 8,000 Neighbours Lose Their Groceries
articles.excerpt: Aleksander Nilaj, who founded the Open Hand Association pantry on Lydig Avenue, was taken into custody on October 13 and is held at Delaney Hall in New Jersey, while supporters petition ICE to release him.
articles.nri_angle: An immigrant-founded Bronx pantry built by an Albanian-American organizer now sits closed after its founder's ICE detention, a case that mirrors how immigrant communities across New York, including South Asian neighbourhoods, run and rely on volunteer food networks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-American Lawmakers Join 63 in Congress Urging Faster Green Cards as Health Coverage Lapses
articles.excerpt: A letter led by Reps. Clarke and Grijalva asks USCIS Director Joseph Edlow for an emergency I-485 expedite pathway after October 1 healthcare cuts left legally present immigrants uninsured while their green cards wait.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American lawmakers Krishnamoorthi, Jayapal and Thanedar joined 60 colleagues pressing USCIS to fast-track green cards for legally present immigrants whose health coverage ended October 1 while their I-485s remain pending.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Immigrant Visas Halve to 26,483 as Restrictions Cover 91 Countries; India Down 16%
articles.excerpt: February 2026 issuances fell to about half the pre-Trump monthly average of 52,000, with immigrant visas for Indians down 16% and employment-based categories the one route still holding steady.
articles.nri_angle: US immigrant visas fell 16% for Indians even though India faces no country ban, while student and H-1B worker visas plunged, directly affecting family reunification and employment pathways for the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 12,700 Indian Tech Professionals Returned From the US in Nine Months, Nearing the 2025 Record
articles.excerpt: Xpheno estimates put returns at 84 percent of last year's record by September, as suspended PERM processing, layoffs and visa uncertainty push mid-career professionals toward India.
articles.image_caption: Travellers pass through Terminal D at Dallas Fort Worth International Airport. Staffing firm Xpheno estimates 12,700 Indian tech professionals returned from the US to India in the first nine months of 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Indian tech professionals in the US are returning to India at a near-record pace, driven by green-card delays and layoffs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two Indians Among 28 Green Card Holders Charged in California Voting Case
articles.excerpt: Amandeep Kaur of Rancho Palos Verdes and Kamlesh Navnitlal Shah of Sacramento are among 28 lawful permanent residents charged in the Justice Department's Operation Protect the Vote. Eleven were arrested Monday; all are presumed innocent.

sources.label: U.S. Attorney's Office, Central District of California

articles.nri_angle: Two of the 28 charged green card holders are Indian nationals, and the case is a direct warning to Indian permanent residents: registering or voting before naturalization can bring felony charges and end a citizenship application.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

Federal government provided list of 28 individuals to California

articles.title: US Proposes Ending Deference on H-1B Extensions, Raising Scrutiny for Indian Workers
articles.excerpt: DHS wants to delete the rule that makes USCIS defer to prior approvals on Form I-129 extensions. The proposal, published October 14 with comments due November 13, would force employers to prove eligibility afresh — and it lands alongside a final rule ending automatic work-permit extensions.
articles.image_caption: A United States flag flies beside a close-up of a U.S. visa. The Department of Homeland Security has proposed removing the rule that requires USCIS to defer to prior approvals on H-1B and other work-visa extension petitions.

sources.label: U.S. Department of Justice, Federal Register Notices 2026

articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals hold the bulk of H-1B visas, so ending deference on extensions would subject Indian tech, engineering and healthcare workers to fresh scrutiny at every renewal even when their job has not changed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Vance Says H-1B Attack Targeted Companies, Not Visa Holders Themselves
articles.excerpt: At a CBS News town hall in Michigan, the vice president said his rhetoric had been imperfect, invoked his South Indian in-laws, and said his criticism was of employers and the visa system — not H-1B holders.
articles.image_caption: US Vice President JD Vance and his wife Usha Vance at a public event. Vance told a Pittsburgh radio interviewer that his H-1B criticism targets companies that undercut American wages, not visa holders, adding that he loves his Indian in-laws.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian H-1B holders in the US, Vance now says the worker is not his target — employers and a visa system that ties status to one job are — but the PERM suspensions and employer scrutiny behind his words remain in force.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ICE Returns Indian National to Oregon Jail to Face Manslaughter Trial Over Fatal Crash
articles.excerpt: Rajinder Kumar, 32, has been indicted on two counts of first-degree manslaughter over a November 2025 crash that killed William Micah Carter and Jennifer Lynn Lower. The charges are pending and have not been tested at trial.

sources.label: US Department of Homeland Security via EIN Presswire

articles.nri_angle: An Indian national's manslaughter trial in Oregon, and ICE's decision to hold deportation until it ends, is a closely watched test of how criminal and immigration cases are sequenced.

articles.title: Vance Walks Back 'Indentured Servants' Remark After India's Strong Protest
articles.excerpt: At a CBS News town hall, JD Vance said his rhetoric was imperfect and that his criticism targeted US companies and the H-1B system, not visa holders — while stressing that the PERM suspensions stand separately from H-1B status.
articles.image_caption: US Vice President JD Vance (file photo)
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals hold over 70% of H-1B approvals; Vance's clarification separates workers from the system criticised, but PERM suspensions still affect green card steps for employees of eight named firms.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UK and Canada Visa Changes Reshape Choices for Indian Students
articles.excerpt: The UK cuts post-study work to 18 months for Graduate applications from January 2027, while Canada caps permits and raises required living funds to CAD 23,448.

sources.label: Passage — IRCC proof of funds update

articles.nri_angle: Indian students must time UK Graduate applications before 31 December 2026 and meet Canada's CAD 23,448 living-funds threshold for applications from September 2026.

articles.title: Taleb Calls H-1B Debate a 'Zero-Sum Fallacy': Foreign Workers Create Jobs
articles.excerpt: The Black Swan author says America's edge rests on other countries' brain drain — and asks whether anti-Indian racism is driving the visa backlash, days after the PERM freeze hit eight major employers.
articles.image_caption: Nassim Nicholas Taleb, author of The Black Swan, who called the H-1B debate a 'zero-sum fallacy' on X.
articles.nri_angle: Indians receive the majority of H-1B approvals, and the PERM freeze at TCS, Infosys, Wipro and HCLTech directly stalls green cards for thousands of Indian tech workers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OCI Cricketers' Fight to Play in India Now Waits on the Centre's Stand
articles.excerpt: Twelve OCI-cardholding youngsters have challenged the BCCI's Indian-passport rule in the Bombay High Court. The court has sought the Central Government's stand, saying any order could have wide ramifications.
articles.nri_angle: The case tests the limits of the OCI card for diaspora families whose children live and train in India: residence rights do not include access to BCCI domestic cricket.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Second Judge Blocks $100,000 H-1B Fee, Including Its One-Year Extension
articles.excerpt: A California federal judge has barred agencies from enforcing the $100,000 payment on new H-1B petitions, ruling that the administration skipped required rulemaking — the second court order blocking a fee the president extended for another year in September.
articles.image_caption: US District Judge Haywood Gilliam in Oakland, who ruled that agencies may not enforce the $100,000 H-1B fee without notice-and-comment rulemaking.
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals, who receive the large majority of H-1B approvals, are the group most affected by whether the $100,000 fee survives in court.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
